title: See where range stops
description: Python range excludes the upper endpoint. Trace loop boundaries, off-by-one errors and the final iteration on a number line.
teacher_summary: Ask the learner to predict the first and last values before running the loop.
student_exercise: Write every value in range(2, 6). Circle the last value, then explain why 6 is excluded.

title: Trace the last iteration
description: Python loop range stopping boundaries and excluded upper limits. Use a trace table to reason about off-by-one iteration mistakes.
teacher_summary: Compare a prediction against a trace table and discuss the stopping condition.
student_exercise: Make a table of values for range(1, 4) and range(1, 5). What changes? Explain which upper boundary is excluded.

title: Follow an accumulator
description: Python iteration, updating totals once per list element and tracking accumulator state through a loop.
teacher_summary: Have the learner update total one step at a time with a short list.
student_exercise: Start total at 0. For each value in [2, 3, 4], add the value to total. Record total after each step.

title: Walk through a list
description: Reasoning about list iteration and accumulation. Track each repeated update and distinguish item values from loop counts.
teacher_summary: Use a hand trace before asking the student to write code.
student_exercise: Trace a loop that counts values greater than 3 in [1, 5, 4]. Show the count after each element.

title: Build common parts
description: Adding fractions requires common denominators, equivalent fractions and equal-sized pieces. Do not add denominators.
teacher_summary: Use equal-sized visual pieces to explain why denominators cannot be added.
student_exercise: Draw 1/2 and 1/3 using sixths. Add the shaded parts and write the resulting fraction.

title: Rename before adding
description: Equivalent fractions and common denominators for fraction addition. Express both quantities in the same unit before combining numerators.
teacher_summary: Ask why one half is three sixths, then combine equivalent fractions.
student_exercise: Rewrite 1/4 and 1/2 with denominator 4. Add them, keeping the denominator unchanged.

title: Scale both quantities
description: Proportional reasoning uses multiplicative scaling. Equivalent ratios require multiplying both quantities by the same factor.
teacher_summary: Contrast adding a constant with multiplying both quantities in a ratio.
student_exercise: A recipe uses 2 cups of rice and 3 cups of water. For 6 cups of rice, how much water keeps the same ratio? Explain the multiplier.

title: Find one unit first
description: Ratios, proportions and unit rates. Divide to find the amount for one unit and multiply to scale both quantities consistently.
teacher_summary: Encourage a unit-rate explanation before cross multiplication.
student_exercise: Four notebooks cost 12 units. Find the cost per notebook, then the cost of seven notebooks.
